summary: Your strongest areas are Project Management, Industry Standards Application, and Technical Communication (all 76%+), showing a solid foundation in professional software development practices. However, Data Structures and Algorithms (71.5%) and Object-Oriented Design (73.5%) remain gaps where consistent feedback highlights the need for clearer reasoning, more complete testing, and tighter links between decisions and implementation. Prioritizing these will build your core technical skills.

priorities.evidence: Attainment 71.5% across CSE2ALG (71.0%) and CSE1OOF (73.5%), with consistent marker feedback across assessments (e.g., CSE2ALG:Central examination: "To strengthen the result, the student should provide clearer reasoning, improve technical precision and show more complete testing or reflection"), indicating persistent gaps in applying algorithms/data structures to problems.
priorities.actions: Revisit CSE2ALG:Central examination feedback to practice justifying algorithm choices with performance measures; redo CSE2ALG:Test exercises on implementing data structures in Java with complete testing.

priorities.evidence: Attainment 73.5% in CSE1OOF, with repeated feedback (e.g., CSE1OOF:Assignment: "Further improvement would come from deeper justification, more consistent evaluation evidence and tighter links between decisions and implementation details") across all assessments, indicating gaps in connecting design to implementation.
priorities.actions: Re-examine CSE1OOF:Assignment feedback to strengthen links between object-oriented design decisions and code implementation; practice CSE1OOF:Test exercises on encapsulation with detailed reasoning.
